title: ‘Knots Landing’ Star Donna Mills Joins OnlyFans at 85 Years Old (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Donna Mills, one of the best known television stars of the 1980s thanks to her role as Abby Cunningham on the CBS primetime soap “Knots Landing,” is
body:
Donna Mills, one of the best known television stars of the 1980s thanks to her role as Abby Cunningham on the CBS primetime soap “Knots Landing,” is throwing fans a surprise by joining OnlyFans  at 85 years old. 

	“I’ve always appreciated the incredible support and encouragement I’ve received from my fans over the years. Social media has been a wonderful way to stay connected, but I’m excited to join OnlyFans because it offers the opportunity for a more personal and direct connection,” Mills said in a statement to Variety. 
	

	The actor will be “sharing moments from my daily life, behind-the-scenes glimpses, and engaging with fans in a more meaningful way” on her new OnlyFans account, adding: “It’s simply another platform to spend quality time with the people who’ve supported me throughout my career while staying true to who I am.”


	“This is not about changing who she is. It is about giving her longtime fans more access to the personality, style and behind-the-scenes moments they already love,” added Andy Bachman, CEO of OnlyFans owner Creators INC. “Donna has always been fearless and ahead of her time. She told me, ‘YOLO — let’s do it,’ and that perfectly captures her attitude. She is approaching OnlyFans on her own terms and creating a space that feels authentic, personal and completely true to her.” 

	Mills got her television start in 1966 with a supporting role on the CBS soap opera “The Secret Storm.” Her role as Madeline Reeves on the ABC soap opera “General Hospital” won her a Daytime Emmy Award for outsanding special guest performer in a drama series. Mills’ recent film roles include “Joy,” “Nope” and “Origin.”
	

	Hollywood talent has been flocking to OnlyFans in recent months. “American Pie” and “Scary Movie” star Shannon Elizabeth launched her own OnlyFans profile in April and earned more than $1.2 million in her first seven days on the platform. She told People magazine that one of the reasons she was pivoting to OnlyFans was because she was growing tired of working in Hollywood where “other people controlled the narrative and the outcome of my career.”

	“My Name Is Earl” Emmy winner Jaime Pressly launched her own OnlyFans profile a few weeks later, explaining: “I’ve always believed in evolving with the times… This is another way for me to connect directly with my audience, on my own terms, with creativity and intention.”

	The awards honors the prop masters and their contributions behind the camera. The winners will be revealed during the live ceremony on Sept. 12.

title: UTA Signs Organization Behind Rose Bowl Game and Rose Parade
description: New Year’s Day came early for UTA, which has signed the Pasadena Tournament of Roses, the organization behind the Rose Bowl Game and the Rose Parade
body:
New Year’s Day came early for UTA, which has signed the Pasadena Tournament of Roses, the organization behind the Rose Bowl Game and the Rose Parade. 

	“The Tournament of Roses proudly produces both the Rose Parade and the Rose Bowl Game, creating one of the most recognized New Year’s Day celebrations in the world,” said David Eads, CEO of the Pasadena Tournament of Roses. “UTA brings deep expertise at a time of rapid change across the media industry, and we look forward to working together to ensure the Rose Parade continues to thrive for generations to come.”
	

	“The Rose Parade has become a defining New Year’s Day tradition for millions of viewers worldwide” UTA Partners Ryan Hayden, Jerry Silbowitz and David Kirsch said in a joint statement. “We’re thrilled to partner with the Tournament of Roses on this iconic event.”


	The Rose Parade is a California New Year’s tradition that has spanned 135 years. The five-and-a-half-mile parade travels along Colorado Blvd. in Pasadena, featuring floral-covered floats, equestrian units and marching bands. The parade is also broadcast across linear and streaming platforms, attracting tens of millions of viewers. 

	The annual Rose Bowl Game started in 1902 and is considered the most prestigious bowl game in college football (its nickname is the “Granddaddy of Them All”). At this year’s game, the Indiana Hoosiers faced off against the Alabama Crimson Tide, with Indiana winning 38 to 3.

	UTA will seek to leverage the Tournament of Roses to seek new opportunities and audiences while preserving the family-friendly tradition.

schema.headline: UTA Signs Organization Behind Rose Bowl Game and Rose Parade

title: Trista Schroeder Named General Counsel and Chief Operating Officer of the Sundance Institute (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Trista Schroeder has been named general counsel and chief operating officer of the Sundance Institute. She will take on her expanded role effective
body:
Trista Schroeder has been named general counsel and chief operating officer of the Sundance Institute. She will take on her expanded role effective immediately.

	Schroeder has served as Sundance Institute’s general counsel since 2020, providing legal and operational counsel through a period of significant institutional change. Most recently, she led the negotiations underpinning the Institute’s request for proposal process that culminated in the selection of Boulder, Colorado, as the new home of the Sundance Film Festival beginning in 2027.
	

	In her new capacity, Schroeder will provide executive leadership across legal affairs, governance, organizational risk management, labor relations, compliance, and organizational administration, serving as a key member of the non-profit’s executive leadership team and strategic partner to CEO David Linde. Continuing to report directly to Linde, she will work closely with executive leadership and the board of directors to strengthen organizational effectiveness, support institutional growth and sustainability, and advance the Institute’s mission — enabling Linde to focus more fully on external leadership, fundraising, strategic partnerships, and organizational vision.


	“Trista has been an indispensable partner to this organization and to me. Her judgment, integrity, and command of the complex and inspirational landscape we navigate have made her a trusted voice in every major decision we’ve made,” said Linde. “Expanding her mandate to general counsel and chief operating officer reflects the full scope of what she does for this Institute — and it allows me to spend more of my time where I’m needed most: with our artists, our partners, and the broader creative community. I couldn’t be more confident in her ability to help lead us through this pivotal chapter, including our transition to Boulder.”
	

	“The board has come to rely on Trista’s counsel not only on legal matters but on the full range of governance and operational questions that come before us,” said Ebs Burnough, Sundance Institute Board Chair. “Simply put, Sundance Film Festival’s new home in Boulder would not have been possible without her — her leadership in negotiating the agreements that brought us there was extraordinary, and the Board is deeply grateful for the discipline and judgment she brought to securing this new chapter. This expanded role formalizes a partnership that has already proven essential to the Institute’s stability and growth.”

	Prior to joining Sundance Institute, Schroeder served as founding executive firector of the Hollywood Commission, working alongside Anita Hill and Kathleen Kennedy to address sexual harassment in Hollywood and advance industry-wide inclusivity and equity. She guided the commission through its start-up phase, set its strategic five-year plan, and executive produced its inaugural Hollywood Commission: Ideas Summit. Earlier in her career, Schroeder served as general counsel to The Team (formerly Wasserman) in Los Angeles, where she helped steer the company’s M&A strategy through the acquisition and integration of more than twelve companies over a five-year window, working with top athletes across the NBA, NFL, MLB, MLS, FIFA, golf, and action sports. She also served as Wasserman’s Chief Administrative Officer, establishing and leading the company’s legal department while driving corporate operations across human resources, crisis management, corporate communications, IT, and real estate.

	Schroeder earned her J.D. at Georgetown University Law Center and served as a law clerk to the Honorable George H. King of the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California. She began her legal career as an associate at Proskauer Rose, where she advised entertainment industry clients on corporate and litigation matters including copyright and trademark enforcement, employment disputes, government investigations, and licensing. Prior to law school, Schroeder was a research producer for Charlie Rose on PBS, and began her career at Morgan Stanley.

title: Artemis Pictures Promotes Four to Executive Roles (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Artemis Pictures, the production and finance company founded by “Dead Man’s Wire” and “Fairyland” producer Siena Oberman, has promoted Ashley TY Cha
body:
Artemis Pictures, the production and finance company founded by “Dead Man’s Wire” and “Fairyland” producer Siena Oberman, has promoted Ashley TY Chao, Maddie Olejnik, Jayden Mann and Nicole Fahel to executive roles.

	Chao has been upped to head of storytelling and innovation, Olejnik is stepping into a creative executive role, Mann into a finance and strategy executive role and Fahel into an operations executive role.


	“We are committed to a future with great cinema,” Oberman said in a statement. “We surround the best in class legacy artists and next generation talent with fresh production strategies and aligned capital targeting modern audiences. Ashley, Maddie, Jayden, and Nicole each bring impressive talent, versatile global experience, positivity, and the discipline our company needs to do that work at scale.”
	

	Chao’s credits include working as an associate producer on “In the Land of Saints and Sinners” starring Liam Neeson. She previously held roles at Legendary Entertainment and Warner Bros. Pictures. Olejnik previously worked at Davis Entertainment and WME, supporting development and setting up meetings with buyers at Hulu, Peacock, NBC, CBS and Focus Features.

	Mann is joining Artemis from a senior financial analyst role at Amazon, where he supported MGM Studios and worked as an extern at UTA, in addition to his previous experience as a production assistant. Fahel has worked on “Fairyland” and “The Good Mother” and served on selection committees for diversity at the Cannes Film Festival and HollyShorts.

	Artemis was founded in 2019. Their credits include “Dead Man’s Wire,” “Fairyland,” “The Good Mother,” “Skin” and “Company.”

title: Marvel, ‘Star Wars’ and DC’s Biggest Fans Discuss Why Their Favorite Franchises Are Struggling: ‘I’m Still Waiting for “Blade”’
description:
James Gunn, there’s a Johnny Depp impersonator who would like to have a word about DC.

	“I think the new ‘Supergirl’ sucks,” 39-year-old Oklahoma C
body:
James Gunn, there’s a Johnny Depp impersonator who would like to have a word about DC.

	“I think the new ‘Supergirl’ sucks,” 39-year-old Oklahoma City native and devoted DC fan John (go figure) says from San Diego Comic-Con’s main floor. He looks exactly like “Pirates” era Depp, with chunky silver rings, a goatee, and a wide-brimmed fedora. Strangely enough, when asked if he’s cosplaying as the Hollywood bad boy, he tells me, as if offended, “Not really.” Returning to what ails DC, he adds, “I think they tried too hard. They’re trying to be like Marvel, and they need to really just be their own thing.”
	

	San Diego Comic-Con is the sweltering core of the sights, sounds and sometimes smells of zealous fandom. It was intense, to say the least, for an SDCC rookie like me. The foot traffic could power a small city for a month, and navigating the convention hall in a sea of sweaty cosplayers felt like front row seats to “The Odyssey” in 4DX. But even for a first-timer, battling overstimulation and dehydration, it was obvious the annual gathering of geeks is ruled by three kings: Marvel, DC and “Star Wars.”


	Once immortal titans of nerdom, the big three have recently lost their grip on the zeitgeist, especially in movie theaters. Marvel, which once set box office records with a snap of an Infinity Gauntlet, is struggling in a post “Endgame” era with relative duds like “Thunderbolts*,” “Fantastic Four” and “Captain America: Brave New World.” DC Studios, under the watch of co-CEOs Gunn and Peter Safran, launched to immediate success with last year’s “Superman,” but saw “Supergirl” flop in June. “Star Wars,” the original blockbuster muscle, returned to theaters after a six-year hiatus with “The Mandalorian and Grogu,” only to be met with a lukewarm reception and lackluster revenues. There have been enough think pieces about why this is happening to fill Stark Tower, but for the real scoop, SDCC superfans told Variety about why their favorite franchises are stumbling and what they can do to reclaim their former glory.
	

	Back on the topic of DC, not everyone was as blunt as John about the studio’s future. Nathan, a 28-year-old Angeleno in a Lobo costume, was “skeptical” when Gunn took control, and feared he’d turn “Superman” into a “Guardians of the Galaxy” sidegrade. However, he “loved” the movie after seeing it for himself, and feels confident Gunn’s vision for DC “is really well intentioned.”

	“I like James Gunn’s mission statement of every movie is going to be a reflection of the character and the writer and director that’s working on it,” Nathan says. “I love that they’re throwing ‘Clayface’ in there. ‘Clayface,’ they’re saying, is gonna be a straight-up horror movie.”

	Nathan suspects the reason “Supergirl” failed was because of a divergence from Gunn’s promised blueprint. THR reported in early July that, due to disappointing audience scores, DC held a bake-off between two versions of “Supergirl” before release. One was from director Craig Gillespie and the other was from the studio. The DC cut won out after earning slightly better results. Nathan, referencing the story, believes giving focus groups the final say is a mistake, since “general audiences don’t know what they want.”

	“They just need something different shown to them. And they are going to like it because it’s different,” he adds. “If it underperforms, at least it was left intact. At least it was the vision.”

	Nathan never mentioned seeing the early “Supergirl” drafts, and it’s impossible to predict what the outcome would’ve been if Gillespie’s cut was chosen. This comment is still significant because it points to the industry-wide disconnect between studios and audiences. Questions about what movies get butts in seats have dominated the business since it emerged from COVID and the dual labor strikes. The problem is not only in the superhero world, but it could feel more significant to superfans like Nathan, considering Marvel, DC and “Star Wars” movies once towered over all others.

	When looking for a dedicated “Star Wars” fan, Jermaine stood out from the rest. Instead of dressing like Obi-Wan, the 36-year-old L.A. native constructed a 14-foot-tall lightsaber cosplay. From the inside of a giant metal hilt, Jermaine told me he’s “hopeful” about the future of “Star Wars,” despite critical and commercial woes. He admits that the recent films are a “mixed bag,” but he considers the Disney+ series “Andor” a “masterpiece.”
	

	Kyle, a 29-year-old San Diego local dressed as a Rebel Commando, isn’t as hot on the “Star Wars” streaming titles. He says having so much content on Disney+ has “oversaturated” the IP, and thinks “Star Wars” would fare better with a methodical, theatrical-minded approach.

	“I think that if [the franchise] returned to the big screen, and had more time to develop and prosper, then it would probably have more of that ‘Star Wars’ root in it,” he says. “It feels like they’re trying to push things out onto a streaming service rather than actually make something grand and adventurous.”

	It’s important to note that neither Kyle nor Jermaine had seen “The Mandalorian and Grogu.” If a man who built a lightsaber suit taller than an NBA basketball hoop didn’t rush to see a “Star Wars” movie after a six-year drought, there could be some truth to concerns that Disney+ has conditioned fans to follow the franchise from home.

	Finally, on to Marvel, which still remains the belle of the ball. The entire weekend is essentially a lead-in to the company’s Saturday Hall H presentation, during which Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige routinely drops news about what to expect from the MCU in the coming years.

	Marvel fans said “soft reboot” and “rebuilding phase” many times while discussing the state of the MCU, but most seemed energized about where it’s heading. Cameron, a 34-year-old from San Diego who dressed as Cyclops for SDCC, finds it “exciting” that Marvel is in a “transitional” period and feels confident it will find a new path forward. Nate, a 23-year-old Spider-Man cosplayer, is likewise optimistic. He’s glad Marvel is past its “filler” era, and is “super excited” to see the worlds of “X-Men” and “The Avengers” collide in December’s “Avengers: Doomsday.”

	“Doomsday” is consequential for Marvel buffs and Disney execs alike. It promises a super team-up of Marvel heroes past and present, obvious hype fuel for fans. Through a more critical lens, many in Hollywood will treat its box office result as a litmus test for Marvel’s health for 2026 and beyond. If “Doomsday” is a big hit, it’s full steam ahead for Feige and friends. If it underperforms, it’s easy to imagine Marvel asking itself, “Now what?”
	

	33-year-old Jordan isn’t so certain about the direction of the MCU. She thinks the Marvel brand, with the success of its animated series “X-Men ‘97” and its popular video game “Marvel Rivals,” is in a “pretty healthy place,” but insists the studio is not. One big reason she is “not that excited for ‘Doomsday’” or much else on the slate is because of “the lack of women.”

	“If you look at the [’Doomsday’] posters, it’s 25 men and five women, and there are a lot of powerhouses, like She-Hulk, for example, that are just totally left out of the cast,” she says. “I feel like the MCU is at a strange point where only some of the shows on Disney+ are good, and nothing else is really exciting.”

	Ferlie, a 56-year-old ex-cop dressed as Sue Storm, hesitates to say Marvel is “trending upward,” since “nothing is going to be like ‘Endgame.’” She also feels “iffy” about Robert Downey Jr. going from Iron Man to Doctor Doom.  However, Ferlie, like many Marvel fans, loves Tom Holland’s “Spider-Man” series, which she says is “in a league of its own.”

	Inside Marvel’s Hall H panel, you’d never think Feige had something to worry about. Fans, most of whom secured a seat at noon to wait for the 6 p.m. show, went berserk when Ryan Gosling was announced as the new “Ghost Rider” and David Jonsson was named the new Black Panther. In the minutes before go time, Journey’s “Don’t Stop Believin’” blasted into the stuffy auditorium, which felt like a not-so-subtle message to any doubters in the room.

	In a post-panel chat, Sophia, a 34-year-old dental receptionist, said she’s gone to SDCC for years, and Marvel’s 2026 Hall H showcase was the “best experience” she’s ever had at the con. Joshua, a 33-year-old school psychologist, thought the panel was “amazing” and mused about how Marvel is masterfully uniting “some of the greatest heroes from the last 20 years” for an ultimate “Doomsday” crossover.

	On the other side of the aisle was Marissa, 28, and Froylan, 57, a father-daughter duo from Murrieta, Calif. They waited since Thursday for their Hall H pass and were left unimpressed by the roughly 40-minute exhibition. Marissa worries that Marvel, instead of executing a meticulous plan, like in the “Infinity Wars” days, is cobbling together a new MCU by “falling back” on IP and stars they “know are successful.” On the “Ghost Rider” reveal, she points out, “Obviously everyone’s gonna love Ryan Gosling.”
	

	One of the only people who skipped IP opinions and identified broader issues was Cyrstal. “Streaming really destroyed a lot,” says the 44-year-old from L.A. She used to be a TV editor and now works as a paralegal. Crystal hates that shows drop an entire season on release day, and thinks streaming has eroded the monoculture that used to propel powerful franchises to billion-dollar heights.

	“I think that art is meant to be consumed together as a culture. It’s more valuable that way,” she says. “Too many streaming platforms, too many series, all at once.” 

	She also believes politics is a major distraction in the entertainment landscape, a phenomenon most recently exemplified during “The Odyssey” press tour. “People are so divided on politics, and everything has to align with, ‘Is this liberal or is this conservative?’ Which viewpoint is it?'”

	Through all the chatter, it was Ruby, a San Francisco construction worker who called me “rude” for asking her age, who best channeled the mixed feelings of Comic-Con’s franchise fans. She said in her post-Hall H reaction, “That’s pretty good. They did put on a show. They always do nice surprises. But we’ve also been promised movies before that never came. So, it’s really cool to see ‘Ghost Rider,’ but are we gonna get ‘Ghost Rider?’ I’m still waiting for ‘Blade.’”

schema.headline: Marvel, ‘Star Wars’ and DC’s Biggest Fans Discuss Why Their Favorite Franchises Are Struggling: ‘I’m Still Waiting for “Blade”’

title: AI Startup Fairground, Founded by Xumo Creator, to Launch First AI-Exclusive FAST Channel (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Colin Petrie-Norris kickstarted a new model of free, ad-supported television through his company Xumo before its reported $100 million-plus sale to
body:
Colin Petrie-Norris kickstarted a new model of free, ad-supported television through his company Xumo before its reported $100 million-plus sale to Comcast. Now, in the era of AI, he’s aiming to reclaim the model with a FAST channel devoted to AI-generated content.

	Fairground Entertainment, Petrie-Norris’ AI studio and distribution platform, is debuting a dedicated FAST channel to what he proclaims is the first to exclusively showcase AI shows and films. Dubbed “Fairground AI Creator TV,” the company plans to launch the channel across five TV and FAST platforms with a 24-hour slate supported by several AI creators, including Kelly Boesch, Kavan the Kid’s Phantom X Studio, filmmaker Ryan Phillips, Wonder Studios and Massive Studios, all of whom Petrie-Norris discovered on social media. (Petrie-Norris would not disclose which platforms are distributing the channel, but promised they’re “the biggest.”)
	

	Petrie-Norris said in an interview that the channel, which will launch next month, merged his passions for television and AI, providing an avenue for creators to showcase the “gorgeous things” they’re creating through a “curated experience.”


	“It’s got massive reach, it’s on a big screen TV,” he said. “It’s not the only thing that we’re doing, but it’s a very powerful way to get massive distribution for all of these creators that, up until now, have had gatekeepers and things get in the way.”

	The channel’s lineup will be programmed by Petrie-Norris and his team in the vein of a traditional TV schedule, with programs slotted in primetime blocks and select specials saved for special events, such as Halloween or Valentine’s Day. He posits that the programs airing on Fairground’s FAST channel are far removed from the minuteslong AI clips proliferating social media platforms due to their attention to story details, with the channel giving them a “voice” to break through.
	

	“These are new names to a lot of viewers,” he said. “It’s not Mr. Beast as our creator. These are the folks in one, two, three years’ time are going to be the Mr. Beasts of entertainment.”

	The move marks a major expansion for Petrie-Norris’ Laguna Beach, California-based startup, which launched last year with five employees, a $4 million seed round from several investors and plans for original shows inspired by the tales of Robin Hood and Dracula. The startup has since grown to 13 employees, and Petrie-Norris hopes the channel marks a new wave of distribution — and, ideally, support — for AI-generated material.

	“It’s fusing some of the very newest technology, right at the vanguard of AI of entertainment, together with a very traditional viewing pattern,” he said. “We’re bringing the best of both worlds together, and make it for a nice experience.”

schema.headline: AI Startup Fairground, Founded by Xumo Creator, to Launch First AI-Exclusive FAST Channel (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Soccer World Cup Boycott Backed Unanimously by All 55 UEFA Members Over FIFA Stake Sale
description: UPDATED: All 55 UEFA member associations have voted to boycott FIFA soccer competitions – including the men’s and women’s World Cups and the Club Wo
body:
UPDATED: All 55 UEFA member associations have voted to boycott FIFA soccer competitions – including the men’s and women’s World Cups and the Club World Cup – if FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s proposal to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors is approved by member associations, according to BBC Sport. The decision came out of an emergency meeting Thursday, days after FIFA announced the plans Tuesday. The first test of the stance arrives in October, when the Women’s World Cup play-offs are scheduled.
	

	UEFA released a statement after the meeting: 


	“UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

	The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

	It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

	National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.
	

	But our opposition goes far beyond process.

	The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

	This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

	Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

	As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

	Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

	There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

	Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

	PREVIOUSLY: Opposition is growing in the soccer world to a plan by the sport’s governing body, FIFA, to spin off its events, principally the World Cup, as a separate commercial entity and invite investors to take a stake in it.

	The new company, FIFA Forward Enterprise, has been valued at about $20 billion. FIFA would seek to sell a roughly 20% stake in the entity. Among the potential investors is Thrive Eternal, led by Joshua Kushner, brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, according to the Financial Times.
	

	Among the opponents of the plan are the sport’s governing bodies in North America and Europe.

	Concacaf, which runs soccer in North America, Central America and the Caribbean, said it was “deeply concerned by the lack of due process” when the plan was conceived. The federation said it was disappointed that the plan has been revealed “before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.”

	UEFA, which runs the sport in Europe, said FIFA’s plan “crosses a line that [soccer’s] governing institutions should never cross.” It added, “The soul and governance of [soccer] are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of [soccer]. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

	UEFA is fast-tracking efforts to hold an emergency meeting of its member associations this week, sources told ESPN, to discuss plans, including a potential World Cup boycott.

	The FIFA plan is subject to ratification by its 211 national member associations. Concacaf represents 41 members, while UEFA has 55.

	Under the plan, funds raised from the sale of a stake in FIFA Forward Enterprise would be used in part to increase annual payments to members from $2 million a year to $5 million. Each would also receive a one-off payment of $20 million.

	FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in a statement, “Every FIFA member association should have an opportunity to seek a fair share of the available funding to shape its own future, deciding for itself rather than relying on others. This is about the democratization of [soccer] worldwide.”

	Among other opponents of the plan are U.K. prime minister Andy Burnham, who said, “The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.”

	Much of the opposition to FIFA’s plan is focusing on the role of Infantino, and his relationship with President Trump.

	Football Supporters Europe, which represents fans, said, “The World Cup is not for sale. Enough of this charade. [FIFA] member associations — and everyone who cares about the future of the game — must stand up to the man who wants to sell world [soccer].”

schema.headline: Soccer World Cup Boycott Backed Unanimously by All 55 UEFA Members Over FIFA Stake Sale

title: ‘Clueless’ Sequel Series With Alicia Silverstone Ordered at Paramount+
description: The “Clueless” sequel series has found a new home. The show, which will see Alicia Silverstone reprise the role of Cher Horowitz, has been greenlit
body:
The “Clueless” sequel series has found a new home. The show, which will see Alicia Silverstone reprise the role of Cher Horowitz, has been greenlit at Paramount+. 

	The project was originally set up for development at Peacock in early 2025, but it was reported in April 2026 that it was no longer moving forward at that streaming service. Sources say that Paramount+ has given the show a six-episode order. It is slated to begin production in Los Angeles in 2027. According to sources, the production has submitted paperwork with the California Film Commission to receive state tax subsidies.
	

	As previously reported, the show will be set in the present day. The logline states, “Beloved Beverly Hills icon Cher Horowitz (Silverstone) has figured out a lot: She’s successful in business and has mastered motherhood—that is, until her daughter’s high school years, and Cher finds that parenting a teenager makes her feel ‘clueless’ all over again.” 


	The greenlight makes sense on a number of fronts. “Clueless” was originally released by Paramount Pictures in 1995, meaning the series will now stay in-house rather than going to an outside streamer. Universal Television was attached as co-studio when the project was set up at Peacock, but will now be produced solely by Paramount-owned CBS Studios.

	In addition, Paramount+ has been in the market for more female-skewing content ever since the Paramount-Skydance merger was completed and Cindy Holland took on oversight of Paramount’s direct-to-consumer business. To that end, Holland’s team has already commissioned the legal drama “Discretion” starring Nicole Kidman and Elle Fanning as well as the limited series “Fear Not” starring Anne Hathaway.
	

	The new “Clueless” series is written by Josh Schwartz, Stephanie Savage, and Jordan Weiss. All three are executive producers, with Schwartz and Savage producing under their Fake Empire banner. Silverstone also executive produces, as does the film’s writer and director, Amy Heckerling, as well as the film’s producer, Robert Lawrence. CBS Studios will produce.

	“’Clueless’ is coming home,” said Jane Wiseman, head of Originals for Paramount+. “Thirty-one years ago, Alicia Silverstone’s Cher Horowitz captivated audiences with her signature chic style, sharp wit and relentless optimism, helping make ‘Clueless’ a box office hit and instant pop culture classic. We’re especially proud to be filming this much-anticipated series in Los Angeles, honoring its starring role in the original film while investing in the city’s exceptional talent and crews.”

	“Clueless” originally debuted in 1995 and is loosely based on the Jane Austen novel “Emma.” Along with Silverstone, the cast included Paul Rudd, Stacey Dash, Brittany Murphy, Donald Faison, Elisa Donovan, Breckin Meyer, and Dan Hedaya. A TV adaptation aired on ABC and then UPN from 1996 until 1999 for three seasons, with Rachel Blanchard playing Cher. The film was also recently added to the United States National Film Registry by the Library of Congress.

schema.headline: ‘Clueless’ Sequel Series With Alicia Silverstone Ordered at Paramount+

title: Disney’s ABC Asks FCC to Reject Petitions to Deny TV License Renewals, Says Agency Is Taking ‘Punitive’ Action Against Broadcasters Trump Dislikes
description: Disney‘s ABC urged the FCC to toss out petitions calling for the agency to deny the renewal of broadcast licenses for ABC’s eight owned-and-operated
body:
Disney‘s ABC urged the FCC to toss out petitions calling for the agency to deny the renewal of broadcast licenses for ABC’s eight owned-and-operated TV stations, and they reiterated the assertion that the agency is targeting the stations with the “death penalty of license non-renewal” because President Donald Trump doesn’t like the programming carried on the network.

	“For years, President Trump has expressly demanded that the Commission revoke ABC’s broadcast licenses for speech he dislikes,” ABC said in an FCC filing submitted July 29 and posted publicly Thursday. “Since his appointment, Chairman [Brendan] Carr has subsequently opened all manner of investigations and issued a slew of burdensome investigatory requests.”
	

	The FCC’s Media Bureau in April issued an order forcing ABC to reapply for spectrum licenses for its eight owned-and-operated stations on an accelerated schedule. The agency claimed it was part of its probe into DEI practices at Disney and ABC — but the move came one day after President Donald Trump called for Jimmy Kimmel to be fired over a joke the late-night host made about First Lady Melania Trump. In May, Disney submitted license-renewal applications for the eight ABC stations, which the company said it did “under protest in response to an unlawful, arbitrary, and unconstitutional order.”


	“For the first time in history, the Federal Communications Commission has ordered an entire group of local television stations commonly owned with a broadcast network to undergo simultaneous license renewal proceedings well before their current licenses expire. That makes these proceedings extraordinary and unprecedented,” ABC said in the latest filing.
	

	The filing continued: “There is no question why the Commission is singling out these eight stations: Each is owned by ABC, and the Administration has openly and repeatedly called for the revocation of ABC’s licenses, because it dislikes the content and viewpoints expressed on ABC network programs.” However, they added, “denying a license renewal for disfavored speech would be outright censorship.”

	In the filing, ABC said the FCC “must deny the Petitions to Deny, or alternatively, dismiss these early renewal proceedings as untimely and unwarranted.”

	“The retaliation against ABC is a signal to every media company in the country: accommodate the Administration’s view of what news coverage should look like or pay the price,” the filing said. “Across the government, regulatory and contracting carrots and sticks have been trained on other disfavored speakers. The tools vary; the objective does not: a media industry too fearful of official reprisal to report the news freely.”

	According to ABC, “The FCC has spent the last 18 months searching for some pretext for revoking the Stations’ licenses. The Commission has found none, because the Stations easily meet the standard for license renewal — which under the law means that the Commission cannot revoke their licenses or order a hearing on their renewal applications.”

	“Calling up the license of a single Station — let alone all eight at once — while the Commission’s DEI investigation has found no violation is unnecessary, premature, and punitive,” the ABC filing said. “Even if any violation were ever substantiated, the Commission has a graduated set of well-established remedies far short of the corporate death penalty of license non-renewal. That the agency reached first for the most extreme sanction in its arsenal, before making any finding at all, reveals its true objective: to chill not only ABC, but every broadcaster watching.”

	Two conservative advocacy groups, the Center for American Rights and the Media Research Center, filed petitions with the FCC requesting ABC’s station licenses not be renewed.

	The Center for American Rights’ petition argued that ABC’s stations are not operating “in the public interest,” alleging the network’s programs “show a consistent and overt partisan bias” and that “ABC engages in explicit racial and gender discrimination”; the group also alleged that “ABC cozies up to the Communist Chinese Party and airbrushes over religious and ethnic cleansing.” The Media Research Center said ABC’s license renewals should be denied because of its alleged “notorious efforts to improperly influence national elections, and its willful engagement in misinformation and the promotion of violence.”
	

	In its reply, ABC said that “the few petitions submitted in opposition to the Stations’ applications come not from their local communities, but from interest groups with a mission to persuade the FCC to exert editorial control over the programming of networks like ABC.” It adds that the petitioners “identify no violation of the Communications Act or FCC rules of any kind, let alone one that could justify the extraordinary remedy of a designation for hearing or denial of a license renewal.”

	RELATED: FCC Slammed by Former Agency Officials Over Review of ABC’s Licenses: ‘An Assault on Free Speech Disguised as Regulatory Process’

	Regarding accusations that ABC programming engages in “news distortion” in violation of FCC rules, ABC said the agency’s policy in this area “provides even less justification for a denial based on statements made on ABC network comedy shows like ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live,’ or opinion commentaries on shows like ‘The View.'” The filing continues, “Even assuming some of the commentary on ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ or ‘The View’ contained factual inaccuracies, ‘isolated mistake[s]’ cannot count as news distortion.”

	The FCC’s deadline for submitting comments opposing petitions to deny ABC’s license renewals was July 29. Replies must be filed no later than Aug. 5. 

	The agency has received more than 153,000 comments on the proceeding — fueled by Disney’s campaign across the eight local stations urging viewers to share comments about the FCC’s review with the agency. ABC’s eight owned-and-operated TV stations are: WABC-TV New York, KABC-TV Los Angeles, WLS-TV Chicago, WPVI-TV Philadelphia, KTRK-TV Houston, KGO-TV San Francisco, WTVD-TV Raleigh-Durham, N.C., and KFSN-TV Fresno, Calif.

	“The outpouring of support for the Stations has been unprecedented for a license renewal proceeding,” ABC said. “Over 140,000 comments have been received from the Stations’ local communities — from individual viewers to local police and firefighters, charities, businesses, and schools — and over 95% support the Stations. These supporters span the ideological spectrum but share a fundamental commitment to free speech and press freedom. This record demonstrates that the Stations serve the public interest with distinction.”
	

	Earlier this week, a bipartisan group of former FCC officials urged the current agency leadership to terminate the “unprecedented” ABC proceeding, which they deemed an unconstitutional abridgement of the First Amendment.

	“This renewal proceeding is the latest attack in a sustained campaign by [FCC] Chairman [Brendan] Carr and the Trump administration of threatening legal sanctions against licensees whose speech President Trump dislikes,” the coalition said in a filing. “And although the purported justification for the early renewal proceeding is that it is in aid of a Commission investigation into unlawful employment discrimination, it is in fact an assault on free speech disguised as regulatory process.”

	ABC also has received support from a consortium of 22 advocacy organizations, including the ACLU and the Electronic Frontier Foundation. “We urge you to continue to defend and exercise your First Amendment rights, so that we can all continue to exercise ours,” the coalition said in a letter addressed to Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro.

	Carr last week said the FCC will consider ABC’s decision to not carry a live broadcast of Trump’s July 16 speech about U.S. election security as part of its review of the ABC station licenses. At a press conference, Carr said, “I’m sure that there are going to be points raised in that proceeding” about ABC’s decision to not air Trump’s speech. “I think that when you have the president of the United States standing inside the White House delivering an important speech, I think that’s something that broadcasters should be carrying,” Carr said. Also at the FCC press conference, Anna Gomez, the agency’s only Democratic commissioner, pushed back on Carr’s assertion that broadcasters are compelled to carry a president’s speech.

	In the FCC proceeding, Disney and ABC have tapped attorney Beth Wilkinson — who is also leading Paramount’s defense in the antitrust case filed by 12 states — alongside Paul Clement and Jennifer Tatel. The legal team is led by Horacio Gutierrez, Disney’s senior executive vice president, chief legal and global affairs officer. The proceeding is FCC Media Bureau Docket No. 26-131.

schema.headline: Disney’s ABC Asks FCC to Reject Petitions to Deny TV License Renewals, Says Agency Is Taking ‘Punitive’ Action Against Broadcasters Trump Dislikes

            Latino also claims Li published Bart's address, photos of his home, property records and information about his family's workplaces ... allegedly exposing Bart and his family to harassment and physical danger.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Bart's lawyer demands Li make her Bart-related posts private while preserving them as potential evidence, stop publishing his personal information and issue a public apology acknowledging she had no factual basis to implicate him in Nolan's death.
      
    
            The clock is ticking ... Latino gives Li five business days to comply ... though he says Bart may sue regardless.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As we reported, Bart recently retained the attorney amid a wave of online allegations linking him to Nolan's death. His family says Bart voluntarily turned over his phone, photos, videos, boat and GPS data to investigators.
      
    
            Latino says law enforcement has NOT identified Bart as a suspect or person of interest ... despite Li's alleged claims.
      
    
            Bart's lawyer says ... "I love when little dogs think they are big dogs. I anticipate at least two more such notices going out by the end of the week. I just bought a new case of toner for my printer."

title: Howard Stern Scores Legal Win, Ex-Assistant's Lawsuit Tossed
body:
Howard Stern
                          Ex-Assistant's $2.5M Lawsuit Tossed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 30, 2026
                            9:05 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Howard Stern scored a big win in court ... with a judge tossing his ex-assistant's entire lawsuit and ruling the NDA at the center of their legal war still stands.
      
    
            According to the decision, obtained by TMZ, the judge rejected Leslie Kuhn's claim that the shock jock's company may have hacked her work email and electronically signed the May 2025 agreement for her.
      
    
            The court pointed to an email sent from Kuhn's account saying, "Signed NDA attached" -- along with the agreement bearing her electronic signature. The judge called her hacking theory a "bald assertion."
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Kuhn also argued she got nothing in exchange for signing ... but the judge noted she kept her job for another nine months, earned more than $192,000 and was awarded an $80,000 bonus.
      
    
            As TMZ reported, Kuhn sued Howard, his wife Beth and their companies, seeking at least $2.5 million and asking the court to free her from confidentiality agreements dated 2022 and 2025.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Kuhn alleged the Sterns treated her like crap while she worked as an executive assistant in their Southampton, NY mansion. Howard called the case a "shakedown" and "transparent sham."
      
    
            Howard had already agreed not to enforce the 2022 agreement ... but the judge upheld the 2025 NDA and dismissed Kuhn's entire lawsuit.
      
    
            The judge didn't sanction Kuhn ... but warned her against making more frivolous arguments.

Emily is not verbal but can communicate with her eyes and by shaking her head -- she understands about 80% of what is going on.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            However, her mom tells us she is improving, getting better day by day, and still fighting to live the best life possible.
      

            As we reported ... Cooper sued Malibu Lighthouse Treatment in 2024, claiming the facility failed to properly care for Emily while she was being treated for ketamine addiction at Summit Malibu earlier that year. This week, they reached a $3 Million settlement -- the defendants denied wrongdoing and did not admit liability.
      
    
            We're told ... Emily is still learning to walk again and needs help being fed -- but she is finally able to sleep on her own and has gotten back to watching movies and shows she enjoys.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            As for her life now ... her mom tells TMZ ... after undergoing more than 10 surgeries, Emily is currently in Mexico working with top-tier therapists ... and the family is hoping to travel to Spain so she can undergo new neurological brain-related procedures designed to stimulate the systems that control speech, communication, and movement.
      
    
            Before her cardiac arrest and subsequent 30-40 minutes without oxygen, Emily was one of the adult industry's biggest stars and won Performer of the Year at the 2021 AVN Awards. She later transitioned into mainstream acting, appearing in the sci-fi film "Divinity."
